title: Who keeps the subsidy?

readouts.l: Consumers' share of each unit's subsidy

predict.q: Start: a subsidy of 2 per unit; PED −0.5, PES 1. Consumers get 2/3 of each unit's subsidy. Demand becomes much more elastic (PED −2), with the same subsidy and supply. What happens to the consumers' share?

options.s: It stays at 2/3, because the subsidy per unit is unchanged
options.fb: The subsidy per unit fixes the total gap, not how it is split. The split follows the elasticities.

options.s: It rises, because more units are now bought
options.fb: More units are bought, but the price falls less on each, so buyers' share of each unit's subsidy falls.
With more elastic demand the price falls less, so producers keep more: the consumers' share falls from 2/3 to 1/3.

task: Move the **Demand elasticity** slider to −2 and watch P1, P2 (= P1 + subsidy) and the two shaded gains.

target.do: Move the Demand elasticity slider to −2 (keep the subsidy at 2 and PES at 1), then press Check.

takeaway: More elastic demand → the price falls less, so producers keep more (consumers' share 1/3) and Q rises more.
